question: Why did David Lewis dismiss the presentist's way of explaining how one person can be both bent and straight?
answer: It discards the person's past and future along with the puzzle. Seated you are bent, standing straight; let only the present shape exist and the contradiction goes, but so does every other time to have a shape at. Nobody believes he has no future, Lewis wrote in 1986, unless at the moment of his execution.
move: A solution that deletes what the problem was about has not solved it.
source: Lewis, On the Plurality of Worlds, 1986
reference: Lewis, On the Plurality of Worlds, Blackwell, 1986, section 4.2
